title: Equations
description: Linear, quadratic, rational, radical, exponential and logarithmic equations.
html:
⚖️ Equations

1. Equivalence transformations

Add/subtract the same on both sides or multiply/divide by the same number $\neq 0$. Linear equations: remove brackets, $x$-terms to one side, divide by the coefficient.

Careful

Never divide by a term that might be $0$: $x^2 = 3x \iff x(x - 3) = 0 \iff x \in \{0, 3\}$.

2. Quadratic equations

$$x^2 + px + q = 0: \quad x_{1,2} = -\frac{p}{2} \pm \sqrt{\left(\frac{p}{2}\right)^2 - q}$$

$$ax^2 + bx + c = 0: \quad x_{1,2} = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$$

Discriminant $D = b^2 - 4ac$

$D > 0$: two solutions, $D = 0$: one solution, $D < 0$: no real solution.

Vieta's formulas

$$x_1 + x_2 = -p, \qquad x_1 \cdot x_2 = q$$

3. Zero-product rule and substitution

$$a \cdot b = 0 \iff a = 0 \text{ or } b = 0$$

Substitution: $x^4 - 5x^2 + 4 = 0$ with $z = x^2$ becomes $z^2 - 5z + 4 = 0$. Don't forget to substitute back!

4. Rational and radical equations

  • Rational equations: determine the domain, multiply by the common denominator, compare solutions with $D$.
  • Radical equations: isolate the root, square, check (squaring creates extraneous solutions).

Example

$$\sqrt{x + 3} = x - 3 \;\Rightarrow\; x \in \{1, 6\} \text{ (candidates)}, \quad L = \{6\}$$

5. Exponential and logarithmic equations

$$a^x = b \iff x = \frac{\ln b}{\ln a}, \qquad \ln x = c \iff x = e^c$$

Isolate the power first. With logarithms: combine, exponentiate, check the domain ($x > 0$).
